Summary: DS Build for Email Outreach
Description:
h2. Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why)

As the Pharmacy Navigator team, we need to extend outreach capabilities to members who do not have a valid phone number but do have a valid email address. Today these members are excluded from Navigator outreach because they cannot be reached through traditional dialer or SMS channels.

We will implement email channel eligibility and template assignment within the Pharmacy Navigator opportunity generation pipeline, including channel determination, cooldown logic, and opportunity deduplication. This will enable eligible members to receive transactional email outreach encouraging them to contact the Navigator Care Team.

This enhancement will expand member reach, improve engagement opportunities, and provide a scalable alternate channel for members who cannot be contacted by phone while maintaining appropriate communication safeguards.

h2. Benefit Hypothesis

If we identify members without valid phone numbers and route them to an email outreach pathway using standardized eligibility and cooldown rules, then we will:

* Increase the number of Pharmacy Navigator members that can be reached through outreach.
* Provide an alternate engagement channel for members who would otherwise receive no outreach.
* Improve inbound callback and engagement opportunities.
* Preserve member experience through deduplication and cooldown controls.
* Establish a scalable framework for future multi-channel outreach strategies.

h2. Contacts / Dependencies

* Data Engineering for channel availability data, pipeline implementation support, and downstream integration.
* HEE for email execution and downstream channel orchestration.
* DEP for email template definitions and template ID management.
* Product and Operations for channel and cooldown policy decisions.
* Compass integration for opportunity visibility and tracking.

h2. In Scope

h3. Member Eligibility

* Identify members eligible for email outreach based on channel availability.
* Validate that members do not have a valid phone number using the Channel Availability table.
* Validate presence of a valid email address.
* Populate channel eligibility flag (flex_field_29) as:
** SMS
** EMAIL
** BOTH
* Preserve existing behavior for members with valid phone numbers.

h3. Opportunity Deduplication

* Ensure a member receives only one outreach record per processing period.
* Deduplicate members with multiple opportunities.
* Select the highest-priority email template when multiple opportunities exist.

h3. Cooldown Logic

* Define and implement email cooldown logic for members routed to email outreach vs phone outreach.
* Prevent members from being repeatedly selected for email outreach within the defined cooldown period.
* Establish rules for how email cooldown interacts with existing Navigator outreach and opportunity generation processes.
* Store cooldown history in a reproducible and auditable manner.

h3. Template Assignment

* Assign email template IDs in flex_field_28.
* Support prioritization rules across opportunity and trigger types.
* Ensure template assignments are traceable and documented.

h3. Pipeline Enhancements

* Modify opportunity generation pipeline to support Email and BOTH cohorts.
* Create channel assignment logic based on Channel Availability data.
* Update outputs required for downstream processing.
* Partner with Data Engineering for integration testing and validation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

||ID||Acceptance Criteria||
|AC1|Members without a valid phone number and with a valid email address are assigned EMAIL in flex_field_29.|
|AC2|Members with valid phone and valid email are assigned according to approved channel assignment rules (BOTH where applicable).|
|AC3|Members without valid phone and without valid email are excluded from outreach.|
|AC4|Channel availability logic utilizes the approved Channel Availability dataset as the source of truth.|
|AC5|A configurable email cooldown rule is implemented and enforced prior to opportunity creation.|
|AC6|Members within the cooldown window are excluded from additional email outreach opportunities.|
|AC7|flex_field_28 is populated with the correct email template identifier based on trigger prioritization logic.|
|AC8|Deduplication results in a single outreach record per member per processing cycle.|
|AC9|Auditability exists for channel assignment, cooldown decisions, and template selection.|
|AC10|Pipeline outputs are successfully consumed by downstream systems without impacting existing Navigator processes.|

h2. Out of Scope

* Email delivery platform implementation.
* HEE execution logic and channel selection rules.
* Email creative development and template design.
* Open, bounce, delivery, and callback reporting.
* Production monitoring and operational reporting.
* Changes to SMS or dialer business logic unrelated to email channel eligibility.

h2. Assumptions

* Channel Availability table accurately reflects current phone eligibility status.
* Email availability information is available within existing source systems.
* Cooldown duration will be finalized by Product and Operations.
* Email outreach is transactional and does not require separate opt-in.
* Existing Navigator opportunity generation cadence remains unchanged.
* Data Engineering will provide support for testing and downstream validation.

h2. Outstanding Questions

* What is the final email cooldown duration (30, 60, 90 days, etc.)?
* Should email cooldown be tracked independently from phone cooldowns?
* Should members in email cooldown still be eligible for phone outreach if phone information becomes available later?
* How should cooldown behave when multiple trigger types are present?
* Should BOTH-eligible members be eligible for email-only fallback after unsuccessful phone outreach?

Summary: Implement Average Resolution Time Metric
Description:
As a Product Analytics stakeholder, I want a standardized definition and calculation for Average Resolution Time so that reporting consistently measures the average time required to resolve identified Pharmacy Navigator opportunities.Business ValueAverage Resolution Time provides insight into how efficiently opportunities are being resolved and allows stakeholders to monitor program effectiveness, identify process bottlenecks, and track improvements over time.Business DefinitionAverage Resolution Time is the average number of business days required to resolve an identified opportunity, measured from the date the opportunity is identified to the date the opportunity is resolved.

Technical DefinitionNumerator:
Sum of the number of days, excluding weekends, between the opportunity start date and opportunity resolved date for all opportunities included in the resolved funnelDenominator:Count of opportunities included in the Opportunity Resolved funnel.

Calculation:
Average Resolution Time =(Total Business Days from Opportunity Start Date to Opportunity Resolved Date) ÷ (Count of Resolved Opportunities)workflow: 1-use interaction fact file to identify the resolve opportunities & get the date resolved using the call end date column2- go to opportunity fact file, find the same resolved opportunities (based on the external opportunity id field)3- for opportunities resolved from the opportunity fact file, use opportunity start date column (this column may need to be formatted to extract the date)4-difference between start date - end date for each opportunity5- sum all differences from step 4 (numerator) this is total business days to resolve opportunities6-count of resolved opportunities (from step 1) this is the denominatorfor manual preparations, we will not consider weekends

Acceptance Criteria:
The metric calculates the average number of business days required to resolve an opportunity.The opportunity population is limited to opportunities included in the Opportunity Resolved funnel.Opportunity start date is used as the beginning of the calculation period.Opportunity resolved date is used as the end of the calculation period.Weekend days (Saturday and Sunday) are excluded from the day count.The numerator represents the total business days between opportunity start and resolution dates for all resolved opportunities.The denominator represents the total count of opportunities included in the Opportunity Resolved funnel.Opportunities without a resolved date are excluded from the calculation.Metric results are validated against a sample dataset to ensure accuracy.Business and technical definitions are documented and available for reporting, dashboard, and ReportADE implementations.Open Questions / Decisions RequiredShould same-day resolutions be reported as 0 days or 1 day?DependenciesAvailability of opportunity start date and opportunity resolved date fields.Finalized Opportunity Resolved funnel definition.Product stakeholder approval of business-day counting rules.Validation support from Product Analytics and Reporting teams.
